title: Optimization Config Audit Events (Safe Apply + Rollback) v0
author: Kevin Osei
content:
> **Archived 2026-01-08:** this page is superseded by "Optimization Config Audit Events (Safe Apply + Rollback)" and is kept for reference only.

## Overview
This page defines the audit event taxonomy for **Optimization Config** lifecycle actions under Safe Apply + Rollback (batching, caching and quantization profiles). It is intended to provide:
- Traceability of actor, time and scope (tenant/model/region/deployment).
- Forensic value via request identifiers, actor identity and diff hash.
- Compliance alignment: SIEM export, consistent retention, least privilege.

Covered deployment modes:
- **Hosted API** and **Dedicated** (Redwood-managed control plane)
- **Private** deployments (operator-managed; same schema, differences noted below)

## Definitions
- **Optimization Config**: versioned object holding runtime optimization knobs (batching heuristics, cache toggles, quantization profile).
- **Config Version**: immutable version record; rollback always targets an earlier immutable version.
- **Active Version**: version currently applied to a scope.
- **Scope**: blast-radius target for apply/rollback (tenant, model, region).
- **Rollout**: staged apply, possibly with canary % and gating.

## Event delivery guarantees
- Events are emitted by the **Optimization Config Service** and the **Rollout Controller**.
- Delivery to the central Audit Log pipeline is **at-least-once**; consumers de-duplicate on `event_id`.
- Cross-service ordering is **best-effort**; correlate with `occurred_at`, `rollout_id` and `request_id`.

## Retention & access
### Redwood-managed (Hosted/Dedicated)
- Default retention: **180 days searchable** in Redwood systems.
- Export to enterprise customer SIEMs via export connectors (see Audit Log Export Pipeline).
- Extended retention (enterprise add-on): **up to 3 years** in cold storage, export-only.

### Private deployments
- Default on-box retention for the audit sink is **14 days** (operator-configurable).
- Customers should forward events to their own SIEM for long-term retention.
- Redwood support may ask for exports during escalations; the customer controls access.

### RBAC
- Viewing audit events in the Console requires `audit.read`.
- Apply/rollback requires optimization operator permissions; audit access does **not** grant action permissions.

## Common schema (all events)
Every Optimization Config audit event MUST carry these fields.

### Required fields (MUST)
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string (UUID) | Unique; used for de-duplication. |
| `event_name` | string | One of the taxonomy names below. |
| `event_version` | string | Payload schema version, e.g. `"1.0"`. |
| `occurred_at` | string (RFC3339) | UTC. |
| `severity` | string | `INFO` \| `WARN` \| `ERROR`. |
| `actor_type` | string | `user` \| `service` \| `system`. |
| `actor_id` | string | User ID or service principal ID. |
| `actor_email` | string | Users only; empty for service/system. |
| `authn_method` | string | `sso`, `api_key`, `service_token`. |
| `rbac_roles` | string | Comma-separated effective roles at action time. |
| `request_id` | string | Control-plane request ID. |
| `source_ip` | string | Client IP; may be empty for internal callers. |
| `org_id` | string | Redwood org/account ID. |
| `tenant_id` | string | Tenant ID. |
| `deployment_mode` | string | `hosted` \| `dedicated` \| `private`. |
| `environment` | string | `prod` \| `staging` \| `dev`. |
| `scope` | string | Canonical scope string (below). |
| `optimization_config_id` | string | Stable config ID. |
| `optimization_config_version_id` | string | Version referenced by the event. |
| `result` | string | `success` \| `failure` \| `partial` \| `queued`. |

### Optional fields (SHOULD when available)
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | Operator or system reason. |
| `change_summary` | string | Short human summary; no secrets. |
| `diff_hash` | string | Hash of normalized diff. |
| `from_version_id` | string | Prior active version. |
| `to_version_id` | string | Target version. |
| `model_id` | string | When model-scoped. |
| `region` | string | e.g. `us-east-1`. |
| `rollout_id` | string | Rollout-related events. |
| `canary_percent` | string | e.g. `"5"`. |
| `gate_set` | string | e.g. `"default-prod"`. |
| `gate_summary` | string | Human-readable gate result summary. |
| `error_code` | string | Stable internal code. |
| `error_message` | string | Sanitized message. |

### Scope encoding (canonical string)
Format:
`tenant={TENANT_ID};model={MODEL_ID|*};region={REGION|*}`

Examples:
- Tenant-wide: `tenant=t_123;model=*;region=*`
- Model in region: `tenant=t_123;model=llama-3-70b;region=us-east-1`

## Event taxonomy
All names live under `optimization_config.*`.

### Version lifecycle
1) `optimization_config.version.created` — immutable version created; SHOULD include `diff_hash`.
2) `optimization_config.version.validated` — schema + semantic validation ran; on failure include `error_code` and `error_message`.
3) `optimization_config.version.promoted` — version promoted to apply candidate; `to_version_id` = promoted version.

### Apply / rollout
4) `optimization_config.rollout.started` — MUST include `rollout_id`, `from_version_id`, `to_version_id`; SHOULD include `canary_percent`, `gate_set`.
5) `optimization_config.rollout.gate_evaluated` — after each gate interval; MUST include `rollout_id`.
6) `optimization_config.rollout.paused` — manual or automatic pause.
7) `optimization_config.rollout.completed` — target version active; `result` = `success`.
8) `optimization_config.rollout.failed` — irrecoverable failure; include `error_code`.

### Rollback
9) `optimization_config.rollback.requested` — `from_version_id` = active version, `to_version_id` = requested prior version; SHOULD include `reason`.
10) `optimization_config.rollback.executed` — rollback applied; `result` `success` or `partial`.
11) `optimization_config.rollback.failed` — include `error_code`.

### Access control
12) `optimization_config.action.denied` — unauthorized create/apply/promote/rollback attempt; `error_code` = `RBAC_DENIED`.

## PII / secrets guidance
- Never log prompts, model outputs, raw payloads, tokens, API keys or private URLs.
- Sanitize `error_message`; prefer `error_code`.
- Keep `change_summary` high level (e.g., “Enable prefix cache for chat routes”).

## SIEM export expectations
- JSON Lines export, stable snake_case field names.
- `rbac_roles` snapshot supports post-hoc authorization review.
- Common customer filters: `tenant_id`, `deployment_mode`, `scope`, `event_name`, `request_id`.

## Implementation notes
- Every Console/API endpoint for create/validate/apply/promote/rollback emits an audit event on success and failure.
- Emit `optimization_config.action.denied` even when the request is rejected before any write.
- Populate `org_id`, `tenant_id` and `scope` consistently; mis-scoping is the main audit risk.
- Private: map operator actions (helm/installer/terraform) to `actor_type=user` where possible, otherwise a dedicated service principal.

## Change control for this spec
- Owner: Security Engineering (audit logging), Product Security approval.
- Adding, removing or renaming an `event_name` or required field requires security review and a backward-compatibility note for SIEM consumers.
